cards.title: Where the credential lives — references/cli-patterns.md §5 and §6
items: tokens live in the OS keystore behind SecretStorePort; never in config, never in logs, never in telemetry, never in --debug output
an env var is a CI path, not the default: secrets never live in config and the token store is the OS keystore

the device-code flow prints the URL and the user code to stderr, polls with the given interval, backs off on slow_down, respects expires_in and writes the token to the keystore without ever echoing it
auth status prints identity, scopes and expiry — no secrets

cards.title: Config precedence — references/cli-contract.md §4
items: managed policy > CLI flags > environment > project local > project > user > defaults
every source is schema-validated and the merged result carries the source of each value, so config get can explain where a setting came from
state under the OS dirs — config, data, cache, state, runtime — written atomically (temp file, fsync, rename) and locked so concurrent instances are safe
migrations are versioned and a downgrade is refused with a clear message; purge removes the local state of a project and secrets are wiped on sign-out

cards.title: Trust and authorization — SKILL.md §10
items: workspace trust: a repository's hooks, plugins, MCP servers and shell-executing settings require an explicit confirmation; --print never silently trusts an arbitrary repo
dangerous flags (--dangerously-*) are loud, policy-gated and refused in an untrusted workspace
authorization is server-side: the CLI may hide an action, the API rejects the request — 3 for unauthenticated, 4 for forbidden with requiredPermission in the error
no remote code, no eval, no new Function: plugins are data plus a reviewed adapter unless the product ships a sandboxed plugin runtime

cards.title: The exit-code contract — references/cli-contract.md §3
items: map every SDK error kind to exactly one code; a new kind is a contract change
3 authentication required or failed · 4 permission denied · 5 not found · 6 conflict · 8 rate limited (honor Retry-After)
a usage error is 2, never 1; a permission denial is 4, never 1 — a script in CI depends on the number
the human message goes to stderr, the JSON error envelope goes to stdout, and the correlation id is shown so support can find the request
